discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and co-workers) predicted in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model and could be driven across a superfluid-Mott insulator transition. In 2002, Greiner and Bloch observed exactly this transition, turning a central model of condensed-matter physics into a clean, tunable experiment. This work started the field of analogue quantum simulation. Bloch and Greiner then built quantum-gas microscopes that image and control single atoms on single lattice sites. These made it possible to observe antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string-like order, many-body localisation and entanglement entropy directly. Zoller's theory work set the conceptual framework and kept anticipating what experiments would do next. Together, their work answers long-standing questions about strongly correlated quantum matter quantitatively, and it now underpins quantum technologies worldwide.
